intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn to say exactly how you feel and talk about the people in your life. You'll choose between -ed and -ing words like confused and confusing, use feelings like proud, relieved and grateful with the right little word after them, and talk about family and relationships: get on with, close to, engaged, divorced. Warm-up: how do you say 'malu' in English?
teachingNotes: -ed vs -ing adjectives: the learner met bored/boring, tired/tiring, interested/interesting and scared/scary in a2-vocab-health, so recap in one line and extend to interested/interesting, excited/exciting, embarrassed/embarrassing, confused/confusing, shocked/shocking, disappointed/disappointing, annoyed/annoying, relaxed/relaxing. Rule: -ed = how a PERSON feels; -ing = the thing (or person) that CAUSES the feeling. A person + -ing is correct but describes the effect on others (My colleague is annoying = he makes people annoyed), so *'I'm very boring in this class' says 'saya orang yang membosankan'. The node's common errors: *'I'm very boring in this class' → bored; *'The news was very shocked' → shocking (news can't feel); *'I'm interesting in music' → interested in. Say plainly that this -ed is NOT past tense. Trick (not a rule): Indonesian me-…-kan (membingungkan, mengecewakan, memalukan) usually matches -ing. Remind: scared → scary (no 'scaring'). Don't test the preposition after disappointed or annoyed (with/in/by/about/at all occur).

Emotions with their prepositions (kata depan): nervous about, upset (about), proud of, jealous of, grateful for (a thing) / to (a person), lonely, relieved, frustrated (frustrating), scared of / afraid of, worried about, angry with (a person, British) / angry at (American, also common in Britain) / angry about (a thing), interested in, excited about. Accept every valid variant and never build a question where two variants are both options: angry with/at, scared/afraid/frightened of, nervous about / nervous of (British). lonely (kesepian, a feeling) vs alone (sendirian, a fact): 'I feel alone' is also natural English, so never test lonely against alone in a 'feel ___' gap.

Indonesian traps: 'malu' is mostly embarrassed (because of something that happened: wrong name, falling over) or shy (a personality: pemalu); ashamed is only for feeling bad about something wrong you did (strong, less common). 'Shame' is a noun: *'I'm shame' is wrong, and 'What a shame!' = sayang sekali, not 'malu sekali'. 'Baper' has no single English word: take it personally (menganggapnya serangan pribadi), (too) sensitive, get emotional. Calling someone else 'too sensitive' can sound unkind: model kind phrases (Don't take it personally, I was a bit too sensitive). Cemburu and iri are both jealous in everyday English (envious is formal).

Relationships and family: get on (well) with (British; American get along with), be close to (sounds 'klous' with an s sound, unlike the verb close 'klouz'), fall out with (argue and stop speaking; past fell out), break up (with) for couples (past broke up), go from single → engaged (to) → get married (to) / be married to (NOT *married with) → divorced / get divorced; in-laws (mother-in-law = ibu mertua, brother-in-law / sister-in-law = ipar); a close friend (teman dekat) vs an acquaintance (kenalan: someone you know a little). Keep it respectful and inclusive: use partner for any couple, keep single and divorced neutral, don't assume a partner's gender, and mention that 'Kapan nikah?'-style questions sound very personal in many English-speaking cultures.

Grammar limits: the chain is A2, so use A0–A2 grammar only (present/past simple and continuous, present perfect, going to, will, present continuous for arrangements, can/could, should, have to). No passive, past perfect, second conditional, relative clauses or reported speech; 'get married', 'get divorced' are vocabulary chunks, not a passive lesson. Don't add idioms (head over heels, tie the knot) or more -ed/-ing pairs (amazed, surprised, frightened) beyond a quick mention unless the learner asks.

keyPoints.title: -ed or -ing?
keyPoints.explanation: -ed = how a person feels (I'm confused, I'm embarrassed); -ing = the thing or person that causes the feeling (This map is confusing, That was embarrassing). New pairs: interested/interesting, excited/exciting, embarrassed/embarrassing, confused/confusing, shocked/shocking, disappointed/disappointing, annoyed/annoying, relaxed/relaxing. Not 'I'm boring in this class' (that means you make others bored), not 'The news was shocked', not 'I'm interesting in music'.

examples.en: I'm confused. These instructions are confusing.
The match was exciting, and the fans were really excited.
examples.id: Pertandingannya seru, dan para penonton sangat antusias.

id.title: -ed atau -ing?
id.explanation: -ed = yang dirasakan seseorang (I'm confused = saya bingung, I'm embarrassed = saya malu); -ing = benda atau orang yang menyebabkan perasaan itu (This map is confusing = membingungkan, That was embarrassing = memalukan). Pasangan baru: interested/interesting, excited/exciting, embarrassed/embarrassing, confused/confusing, shocked/shocking, disappointed/disappointing, annoyed/annoying, relaxed/relaxing. Bukan 'I'm boring in this class' (artinya kamu membuat orang lain bosan), bukan 'The news was shocked', bukan 'I'm interesting in music'.

keyPoints.title: More feelings and their prepositions
keyPoints.explanation: nervous, upset, proud of, jealous of, grateful for, lonely, relieved, frustrated, scared of, worried about, angry with, interested in. Many feelings need a fixed small word after them (a preposition), and it often doesn't match Indonesian: bangga pada = proud of. 'Malu' is usually embarrassed (something happened) or shy (personality), not shame. 'Baper' has no one word: take it personally, too sensitive.

examples.en: I was really relieved when the test results came back.
examples.id: Saya benar-benar lega saat hasil tesnya keluar.

examples.en: Don't take it personally. He's like that with everyone.
examples.id: Jangan baper. Dia memang begitu ke semua orang.

id.title: Perasaan lain dan kata depannya
id.explanation: nervous, upset, proud of, jealous of, grateful for, lonely, relieved, frustrated, scared of, worried about, angry with, interested in. Banyak kata perasaan butuh kata kecil tetap sesudahnya (kata depan / preposition), dan sering tidak sama dengan bahasa Indonesia: bangga pada = proud of. 'Malu' biasanya embarrassed (karena suatu kejadian) atau shy (sifat pemalu), bukan shame. 'Baper' tidak punya satu kata: take it personally, too sensitive.

keyPoints.title: Relationships and family
keyPoints.explanation: get on (well) with (akur), be close to (dekat), fall out with (bertengkar lalu tidak saling bicara), break up (putus), single, engaged, get married, be married to (not 'married with'), divorced, in-laws (mertua, ipar), partner, a close friend vs an acquaintance (kenalan).

examples.id: Saya akur dengan rekan-rekan kerja saya.

examples.en: My sister is married to a nurse from Makassar.
examples.id: Kakak perempuanku menikah dengan seorang perawat dari Makassar.

examples.en: My parents got divorced when I was ten.
examples.id: Orang tuaku bercerai waktu aku berumur sepuluh tahun.

id.title: Hubungan dan keluarga
id.explanation: get on (well) with (akur dengan), be close to (dekat dengan), fall out with (bertengkar lalu tidak saling bicara), break up (putus), single (lajang), engaged (bertunangan), get married (menikah), be married to (sudah menikah dengan; bukan 'married with'), divorced (bercerai), in-laws (mertua, ipar), partner (pasangan), a close friend (teman dekat) vs an acquaintance (kenalan).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: I'm interesting in Korean dramas, so I'm learning Korean.

i am interested in korean dramas so i am learning korean
i'm interested in korean dramas so i am learning korean

i am interested in korean dramas
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm interested in Korean dramas, so I'm learning Korean (how I feel → -ed; interested + in). Writing only the corrected first part = full marks. 'I'm interested on/about Korean dramas' = 50 (right adjective, wrong preposition). 'I interested in…' (no am) = 60. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the missing word: My parents are really proud ___ my little brother. He won a scholarship to study in Japan.
assessment.rubric: Correct: of (proud of = bangga pada). 'on', 'with', 'for' or 'about' = 0 (word-by-word from 'pada' or guesses).

assessment.prompt: Budi called his new manager by the wrong name in a meeting, and everyone laughed. He felt very 'malu'. Complete with one English word: Budi felt really ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: embarrassed (malu because of something that happened). 'embarassed' / 'embarrased' (one letter missing) = 80. 'embarrassing' = 30 (that describes the situation, not Budi). 'shy' = 30 (shy is a personality, not a moment). 'ashamed' = 30 (for doing something morally wrong). 'humiliated' = 70 (much stronger than malu here). 'stupid' or 'silly' = 50 (natural, but not the word for malu). 'shame' = 0 (a noun).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: I get on really well ___ my mother-in-law. We often cook together on Sundays.
assessment.rubric: Correct: with (get on well with someone = akur dengan). 'to' = 0. 'along' = 30 (American get along with needs with too, and the gap is after well).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: My cousin is married with a man from Australia.
acceptableAnswers: my cousin is married to a man from australia
my cousin's married to a man from australia
my cousin married a man from australia
assessment.rubric: Correct: My cousin is married to a man from Australia (be married to someone; 'married with' is the Indonesian 'menikah dengan' translated word by word). 'My cousin married a man from Australia' is also fully correct. 'married by' or 'married at' = 0. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: I don't know Pak Hasan very well. We've only met twice at work conferences. He's an ___, not a close friend.
assessment.rubric: Correct: acquaintance (kenalan: someone you know a little). Small spelling slips like 'aquaintance' or 'acquaintence' = 80. 'friend' or 'a colleague' = 0 (doesn't fit 'an' / 'not a close friend').

material.title: -ed or -ing: who feels it, and what causes it

blocks.text:
You met **bored / boring** in the health lesson: **I'm bored** (saya bosan), but **this film is boring** (membosankan). The same rule works for many more **adjectives** (words that describe a person or a thing, like *happy* or *big*):

- **-ed** = how a **person feels**: *I'm confused* = saya bingung.
- **-ing** = the thing (or person) that **causes** the feeling: *This map is confusing* = peta ini membingungkan.

Careful: this **-ed** is **not** past tense. *I'm bored* is about now; it just describes your feeling.

Here are eight new pairs. Each line shows the person who feels it, then the thing that causes it:

id.text:
Kamu sudah kenal **bored / boring** di pelajaran kesehatan: **I'm bored** (saya bosan), tapi **this film is boring** (film ini membosankan). Aturan yang sama berlaku untuk banyak **kata sifat** lain (adjective: kata yang menjelaskan orang atau benda, seperti *happy* atau *big*):

- **-ed** = yang **dirasakan seseorang**: *I'm confused* = saya bingung.
- **-ing** = benda (atau orang) yang **menyebabkan** perasaan itu: *This map is confusing* = peta ini membingungkan.

Hati-hati: **-ed** di sini **bukan** bentuk lampau. *I'm bored* itu tentang sekarang; kata ini hanya menjelaskan perasaanmu.

Ini delapan pasangan baru. Tiap baris menunjukkan orang yang merasakan, lalu benda yang menyebabkannya:

rows.en: I'm interested in history. History is interesting.
rows.id: Saya tertarik pada sejarah. Sejarah itu menarik.

rows.en: The kids are excited about the holiday. The trip will be exciting.
rows.id: Anak-anak antusias soal liburan. Perjalanannya pasti seru.

rows.en: I was embarrassed. My mistake was so embarrassing.
rows.id: Saya malu. Kesalahanku memalukan sekali.

rows.en: I'm confused. The new KRL map is confusing.
rows.id: Saya bingung. Peta KRL yang baru membingungkan.

rows.en: Everyone was shocked. The price was shocking.
rows.id: Semua orang kaget. Harganya mengejutkan.

rows.en: The fans were disappointed. The result was disappointing.
rows.id: Para penggemar kecewa. Hasilnya mengecewakan.

rows.en: I get annoyed in traffic jams. The noise is annoying.
rows.id: Saya kesal kalau macet. Suaranya menyebalkan.

rows.en: I feel relaxed now. The massage was really relaxing.
rows.id: Sekarang saya merasa santai. Pijatnya benar-benar bikin rileks.

blocks.text:
**Trick:** Indonesian often shows the same thing. When the Indonesian word has **me-…-kan** (*membingungkan, mengecewakan, memalukan, menyebalkan*), English usually uses **-ing**. It's only a trick, not a rule: *menarik* (interesting) has no -kan.

**A person can be -ing too**, and that isn't a mistake: *My colleague is annoying* = he makes **other people** annoyed. So `I'm very boring in this class` says *saya orang yang sangat membosankan*! Say **I'm very bored in this class.** In the same way, news can't feel anything: `The news was shocked` → **The news was shocking.**

And `I'm interesting in music` → **I'm interested in music** (tertarik **pada** musik = interested **in**).

Remember the exception from A2: scared → **scary** (menakutkan), never *scaring*.

id.text:
**Trik:** bahasa Indonesia sering menunjukkan hal yang sama. Kalau kata Indonesianya berbentuk **me-…-kan** (*membingungkan, mengecewakan, memalukan, menyebalkan*), bahasa Inggrisnya biasanya **-ing**. Ini cuma trik, bukan aturan: *menarik* (interesting) tidak pakai -kan.

**Orang juga bisa -ing**, dan itu bukan kesalahan: *My colleague is annoying* = dia membuat **orang lain** kesal (dia menyebalkan). Jadi `I'm very boring in this class` artinya *saya orang yang sangat membosankan*! Katakan **I'm very bored in this class.** Sama halnya, berita tidak bisa merasakan apa-apa: `The news was shocked` → **The news was shocking** (beritanya mengejutkan).

Lalu `I'm interesting in music` → **I'm interested in music** (tertarik **pada** musik = interested **in**).

Ingat pengecualian dari A2: scared → **scary** (menakutkan), bukan *scaring*.

blocks.prompt: Everyone hoped for a happy ending, but the hero dies. The ending of the film was ___.
blocks.explain: The ending **causes** the feeling (mengecewakan), so use **-ing**: disappointing. The people watching were *disappointed*.

id.prompt: Semua orang berharap akhir yang bahagia, tapi tokoh utamanya meninggal. Lengkapi: The ending of the film was ___.
id.explain: Akhir ceritanya yang **menyebabkan** perasaan (mengecewakan), jadi pakai **-ing**: disappointing. Penontonnya yang *disappointed* (kecewa).

id.title: -ed atau -ing: siapa yang merasa, apa penyebabnya

blocks.text:
More words for feelings:

- **nervous** = gugup, deg-degan; **upset** = sedih atau kesal karena sesuatu terjadi
- **proud** = bangga; **jealous** = iri, cemburu; **grateful** = bersyukur, berterima kasih
- **lonely** = kesepian; **relieved** = lega (a worry has gone away)
- **frustrated** = frustrasi, kesal karena terus gagal (the cause is *frustrating*)
- **scared** / **afraid** = takut

Many feelings need a fixed little word after them, a **preposition** (kata depan, like *of, about, in, with, for*). It often doesn't match Indonesian, so learn the pair as one chunk:

- proud **of**, jealous **of**, scared **of** (bangga **pada**, iri **pada**, takut **pada**: not *proud on*)
- worried **about**, nervous **about**, excited **about**
- interested **in**
- grateful **for** something, grateful **to** someone
- angry **with** a person (British) / angry **at** a person (American, common in Britain too), angry **about** a thing

id.text:
Kata-kata perasaan lainnya:

- **nervous** = gugup, deg-degan; **upset** = sedih atau kesal karena sesuatu terjadi
- **proud** = bangga; **jealous** = iri, cemburu; **grateful** = bersyukur, berterima kasih
- **lonely** = kesepian; **relieved** = lega (rasa khawatirnya hilang)
- **frustrated** = frustrasi, kesal karena terus gagal (penyebabnya *frustrating*)
- **scared** / **afraid** = takut

Banyak kata perasaan butuh kata kecil tetap sesudahnya, yaitu **kata depan** (preposition, seperti *of, about, in, with, for*). Sering tidak sama dengan bahasa Indonesia, jadi hafalkan pasangannya sebagai satu paket:

- proud **of**, jealous **of**, scared **of** (bangga **pada**, iri **pada**, takut **pada**: bukan *proud on*)
- worried **about**, nervous **about**, excited **about**
- interested **in**
- grateful **for** sesuatu, grateful **to** seseorang
- angry **with** orang (Britania) / angry **at** orang (Amerika, sering juga di Inggris), angry **about** sesuatu

rows.en: Sari is nervous about her job interview tomorrow.
rows.id: Sari deg-degan soal wawancara kerjanya besok.

rows.en: My mum was upset when I forgot her birthday.
rows.id: Ibuku sedih waktu aku lupa ulang tahunnya.

rows.en: We're so proud of you!
rows.id: Kami bangga sekali padamu!

rows.en: I'm grateful to my teachers for their patience.
rows.id: Saya berterima kasih kepada guru-guru saya atas kesabaran mereka.
rows.note: to a person, for a thing

rows.en: Living alone in a new city can be lonely.
rows.id: Tinggal sendirian di kota baru bisa bikin kesepian.

rows.en: I'm frustrated. This printer never works!
rows.id: Aku frustrasi. Printer ini nggak pernah beres!

blocks.text:
**alone or lonely?** **alone** = sendirian, just a fact: *I live alone* (and maybe you love it). **lonely** = kesepian, a sad feeling: *I feel lonely at the weekend.* You can be alone and happy, or lonely in a crowd.

Not every feeling has an -ed / -ing pair: *nervous, proud, jealous, grateful, lonely* don't. And **upset** has no -ed: `I'm upsetted` is wrong; say **I'm upset**.

id.text:
**alone atau lonely?** **alone** = sendirian, hanya fakta: *I live alone* (dan mungkin kamu senang begitu). **lonely** = kesepian, perasaan sedih: *I feel lonely at the weekend.* Kamu bisa sendirian tapi bahagia, atau kesepian di tengah keramaian.

Tidak semua kata perasaan punya pasangan -ed / -ing: *nervous, proud, jealous, grateful, lonely* tidak punya. Dan **upset** tidak pakai -ed: `I'm upsetted` salah; katakan **I'm upset**.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan's mother is in hospital. He is very worried ___ her.
blocks.explain: The chunk is **worried about** (khawatir tentang). *worried of* and *worried with* aren't used.

id.prompt: Ibu Pak Hasan dirawat di rumah sakit. Lengkapi: He is very worried ___ her.
id.explain: Paketnya **worried about** (khawatir tentang). *worried of* dan *worried with* tidak dipakai.

material.title: Malu, baper and other Indonesian traps

blocks.text:
**Malu** is not one English word. Choose by the situation:

- **embarrassed** = malu because of **something that happened**: you called someone by the wrong name, you fell over in the office. The situation is **embarrassing** (memalukan).
- **shy** = malu as a **personality**: a person who is quiet with new people (pemalu, malu-malu).
- **ashamed** = malu because **you did something wrong** (merasa bersalah). It's strong and less common: *I'm ashamed of what I said.*

Careful: **shame** is a noun (a thing), not a feeling word, so `I'm shame` is wrong. And **What a shame!** means *sayang sekali!*, not *malu sekali*.

**Baper** (bawa perasaan) has no single English word. Say:
- **take it personally** = menganggapnya serangan pribadi: *Don't take it personally.*
- **(too) sensitive** = gampang tersinggung: *I was a bit too sensitive yesterday.*
- **get emotional** = jadi emosional, terbawa perasaan.

**Cemburu** and **iri** are both **jealous** in everyday English: *He's jealous of his brother.*

id.text:
**Malu** bukan satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris. Pilih sesuai situasinya:

- **embarrassed** = malu karena **sesuatu yang terjadi**: kamu salah menyebut nama orang, kamu jatuh di kantor. Situasinya **embarrassing** (memalukan).
- **shy** = malu sebagai **sifat**: orang yang pendiam dengan orang baru (pemalu, malu-malu).
- **ashamed** = malu karena **kamu berbuat salah** (merasa bersalah). Kata ini kuat dan lebih jarang: *I'm ashamed of what I said.*

Hati-hati: **shame** adalah kata benda (sebuah hal), bukan kata perasaan, jadi `I'm shame` salah. Dan **What a shame!** artinya *sayang sekali!*, bukan *malu sekali*.

**Baper** (bawa perasaan) tidak punya satu kata bahasa Inggris. Katakan:
- **take it personally** = menganggapnya serangan pribadi: *Don't take it personally.*
- **(too) sensitive** = gampang tersinggung: *I was a bit too sensitive yesterday.*
- **get emotional** = jadi emosional, terbawa perasaan.

**Cemburu** dan **iri** sama-sama **jealous** dalam bahasa Inggris sehari-hari: *He's jealous of his brother.*

rows.en: I fell over in front of the whole office. It was so embarrassing!
rows.id: Aku jatuh di depan seluruh kantor. Malu banget!

rows.en: Our daughter is a bit shy with new people.
rows.id: Anak perempuan kami agak pemalu dengan orang baru.

rows.en: You can't come to the wedding? What a shame!
rows.id: Kamu nggak bisa datang ke pernikahannya? Sayang sekali!

rows.en: Sorry, I was a bit too sensitive yesterday.
rows.id: Maaf, kemarin aku agak baper.

id.note: pakai untuk diri sendiri, lebih sopan

blocks.text: Be kind with these words. Saying *You're too sensitive* to someone who is upset can sound rude. It's softer to say **Don't take it personally** or to talk about yourself: **I was a bit too sensitive.**

id.text: Pakai kata-kata ini dengan baik. Bilang *You're too sensitive* (kamu baper banget) ke orang yang sedang sedih bisa terdengar kasar. Lebih halus bilang **Don't take it personally** atau bicara tentang dirimu sendiri: **I was a bit too sensitive.**

blocks.prompt: Tono's colleague got a promotion and a big bonus. Tono wants the same things, and he isn't happy for her. Tono is ___ of her.
blocks.explain: Wanting what someone else has is **jealous** (iri). *proud of her* would mean he's happy for her success, but he isn't; *grateful* is for help you get.

id.prompt: Rekan kerja Tono naik jabatan dan dapat bonus besar. Tono ingin hal yang sama, dan dia tidak ikut senang. Lengkapi: Tono is ___ of her.
id.explain: Ingin memiliki apa yang dimiliki orang lain adalah **jealous** (iri). *proud of her* berarti dia ikut bangga, padahal tidak; *grateful* untuk bantuan yang kamu terima.

blocks.text:
**How people get on** (these are phrasal verbs: a verb + a small word, with a new meaning):
- **get on (well) with** someone = akur dengan. American English: **get along with**.
- **be close to** someone = dekat dengan. Here *close* sounds like 'klous' with an **s** sound, not like the verb *close the door* ('klouz').
- **fall out with** someone = bertengkar lalu tidak saling bicara (past: *fell out*).

**Couples:**
- **single** = lajang, tidak punya pasangan; **a partner** = pasangan (for any couple, married or not)
- **engaged** (to) = bertunangan → **get married** (to) = menikah → **be married to** = sudah menikah dengan
- **break up** (with) = putus (past: *broke up*); **divorced** = bercerai: *They got divorced.*

**Family by marriage:** your **in-laws** = keluarga pasanganmu: **mother-in-law / father-in-law** = ibu / bapak mertua, **brother-in-law / sister-in-law** = ipar.

**Friends:** Indonesian *teman* covers a lot. English separates **a close friend** (teman dekat, sahabat) and **an acquaintance** (kenalan: someone you know a little).

id.text:
**Bagaimana hubungan orang** (ini phrasal verb: kata kerja + kata kecil, dengan arti baru):
- **get on (well) with** seseorang = akur dengan. Bahasa Inggris Amerika: **get along with**.
- **be close to** seseorang = dekat dengan. Di sini *close* dibaca 'klous' dengan bunyi **s**, bukan seperti kata kerja *close the door* ('klouz').
- **fall out with** seseorang = bertengkar lalu tidak saling bicara (lampau: *fell out*).

**Pasangan:**
- **single** = lajang, tidak punya pasangan; **a partner** = pasangan (untuk pasangan mana pun, menikah atau tidak)
- **engaged** (to) = bertunangan → **get married** (to) = menikah → **be married to** = sudah menikah dengan
- **break up** (with) = putus (lampau: *broke up*); **divorced** = bercerai: *They got divorced.*

**Keluarga karena pernikahan:** **in-laws** = keluarga pasanganmu: **mother-in-law / father-in-law** = ibu / bapak mertua, **brother-in-law / sister-in-law** = ipar.

**Teman:** kata *teman* dalam bahasa Indonesia cakupannya luas. Bahasa Inggris membedakan **a close friend** (teman dekat, sahabat) dan **an acquaintance** (kenalan: orang yang kamu kenal sedikit).

rows.en: Do you get on well with your boss?
rows.id: Kamu akur dengan bosmu?

rows.en: I'm very close to my grandmother.
rows.id: Saya sangat dekat dengan nenek saya.

rows.en: Dimas and his girlfriend broke up last year.
rows.id: Dimas dan pacarnya putus tahun lalu.

rows.en: Bu Ani is married to a teacher from Medan.
rows.id: Bu Ani menikah dengan seorang guru dari Medan.

rows.en: We're spending Lebaran with my in-laws in Solo.
rows.id: Kami berlebaran bersama keluarga mertua di Solo.

rows.en: My brother is single, and he's happy that way.
rows.id: Kakakku masih lajang, dan dia senang begitu.

blocks.text:
**menikah dengan** → **married to**, not `married with` (*married with children* means *sudah menikah dan punya anak*). You can also say **She married a doctor** with no little word.

**Respectful small talk:** in many English-speaking cultures, questions like *Kapan nikah?* (When are you getting married?) or *Why are you still single?* feel very personal. Talk about people kindly: **partner** works for any couple, and *single* or *divorced* are just facts, not bad words.

id.text:
**menikah dengan** → **married to**, bukan `married with` (*married with children* artinya *sudah menikah dan punya anak*). Kamu juga bisa bilang **She married a doctor** tanpa kata kecil.

**Basa-basi yang sopan:** di banyak budaya berbahasa Inggris, pertanyaan seperti *Kapan nikah?* (When are you getting married?) atau *Kok masih single?* terasa sangat pribadi. Bicarakan orang dengan baik: **partner** cocok untuk pasangan mana pun, dan *single* atau *divorced* hanyalah fakta, bukan kata yang buruk.

blocks.prompt: Rina and her sister talk every day and tell each other everything. They're very ___.
blocks.explain: For people, **close** means *dekat* in feelings (said 'klous'). *near* is only about distance, and *closed* means *tutup* (a shop is closed).

id.prompt: Rina dan kakaknya mengobrol setiap hari dan saling menceritakan semuanya. Lengkapi: They're very ___.
id.explain: Untuk orang, **close** berarti *dekat* secara perasaan (dibaca 'klous'). *near* hanya soal jarak, dan *closed* berarti *tutup* (tokonya tutup).

suggestedQuestions: Can a person be 'boring' or only things?
How do I say 'malu' and 'baper' in English?
What's the difference between a friend and an acquaintance?

resources.title: Bored or Boring? Learn about -ED and -ING adjectives in English
resources.note: Adam explains -ed and -ing adjectives as cause and effect: the -ing thing causes the feeling, the -ed person has it. All in English, for beginner to intermediate learners, with a quiz on the engVid site.

id.note: Adam menjelaskan kata sifat -ed dan -ing sebagai sebab dan akibat: benda -ing menyebabkan perasaan, orang -ed yang merasakannya. Seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris, untuk tingkat pemula sampai menengah, dengan kuis di situs engVid.

resources.title: Adjectives ending in '-ed' and '-ing'
resources.note: A short explanation and two quizzes with many of this lesson's pairs (annoyed, confused, disappointed, excited, interested). You may know the page from the health lesson: try the quizzes again with the new pairs.

id.note: Penjelasan singkat dan dua kuis dengan banyak pasangan dari pelajaran ini (annoyed, confused, disappointed, excited, interested). Mungkin kamu sudah kenal halaman ini dari pelajaran kesehatan: coba kuisnya lagi dengan pasangan-pasangan baru.

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar mengatakan dengan tepat apa yang kamu rasakan dan membicarakan orang-orang di hidupmu. Kamu akan memilih antara kata -ed dan -ing seperti confused dan confusing, memakai kata perasaan seperti proud, relieved dan grateful dengan kata kecil yang tepat sesudahnya, dan membicarakan keluarga serta hubungan: get on with, close to, engaged, divorced. Pemanasan: apa bahasa Inggrisnya 'malu'?
suggestedQuestions: Apakah orang bisa disebut 'boring', atau hanya benda?

assessment.fl-1: Lengkapi dengan bentuk kata shock yang tepat: The news about the flood in Bekasi was really ___. Nobody expected so much rain.
assessment.fl-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: I'm interesting in Korean dramas, so I'm learning Korean.
assessment.fl-3: Lengkapi dengan kata yang hilang: My parents are really proud ___ my little brother. He won a scholarship to study in Japan.
assessment.fl-4: Budi salah menyebut nama manajer barunya di rapat, dan semua orang tertawa. Dia merasa sangat malu. Lengkapi dengan satu kata bahasa Inggris: Budi felt really ___.
assessment.fl-5: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: I get on really well ___ my mother-in-law. We often cook together on Sundays.
assessment.fl-6: Perbaiki kesalahannya: My cousin is married with a man from Australia.
assessment.fl-7: Lengkapi dengan satu kata bahasa Inggris: I don't know Pak Hasan very well. We've only met twice at work conferences. He's an ___, not a close friend.
